rules.title: Utility payment defense to nonpayment eviction
rules.requirement: A tenant may not be evicted for nonpayment of rent if the unpaid rent was used to keep utility services (electric, gas, water, sewer) on after notice of discontinuance, where the landlord was responsible for those utilities and did not pay. The money used counts as part of the rent payment.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants facing eviction for nonpayment where the landlord was responsible for paying utility services.
rules.quoted_span: Note: A tenant may not be evicted for nonpayment of rent, if the tenant used the unpaid portion of rent to continue utility services to the rental premises after receiving notice that the services were in danger of being discontinued, and if the landlord was responsible for the payment of those utility services and did not make the payments required to retain the us e of those services.

rules.title: Disorderly conduct eviction ground
rules.requirement: A landlord may file for eviction if, after a written Notice to Cease, the tenant continues disorderly conduct that destroys the peace and quiet of other tenants or the neighborhood. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days before filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants who continue disorderly conduct after a written Notice to Cease.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(b)).

rules.title: Damage or destruction to the property eviction ground
rules.requirement: A tenant may be evicted for intentionally or through gross negligence causing or allowing destruction, damage, or injury to the property, with a Notice to Quit served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days before filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants who intentionally or by gross negligence damage the property.
rules.quoted_span: The tenant may be evicted if they have intentionally or by reason of gross negligence caused or allowed destruction, damage, or injury to the property.

rules.title: Substantial violation of landlord's rules and regulations
rules.requirement: After a written Notice to Cease, a landlord may file for eviction if the tenant continues to substantially violate reasonable rules in the lease or accepted in writing. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing, on or before the start of a new month.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month before filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants who substantially violate reasonable rules and regulations after a Notice to Cease.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for eviction. In addition, any notices must be given on or before the start of a new month (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(d)).

rules.title: Violation of lease covenants with right of re-entry
rules.requirement: If the tenant continues to substantially breach reasonable lease covenants after a written Notice to Cease and the lease reserves a right of re-entry, the landlord may file for eviction after serving a Notice to Quit at least one month before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month before filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants whose lease reserves a right of re-entry and who substantially breach lease covenants.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for this type of eviction.

rules.title: Public housing lease violation for drug or illegal activity
rules.requirement: In public housing, a landlord may file for eviction for substantial breach of lease covenants on illegal drug use or other illegal activities; the covenant must conform to federal guidelines and be in effect at the start of the lease, and no Notice to Cease is required before the Notice to Quit.
rules.coverage_text: Public housing tenants.
rules.quoted_span: The covenant or agreement must conform to federal guidelines and must have been in effect at the beginning of the lease term. The landlord does not have to give Notice to Cease the illegal activity before filing a Notice to Quit.
rules.interaction_text: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant in accordance with federal regulations pertaining to public housing

rules.title: Failure to pay rent increase
rules.requirement: A landlord may file for eviction if the tenant fails to pay rent after notice of a rent increase and a Notice to Quit; the increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with other laws including rent control. The Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month before filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants who fail to pay a rent increase after notice.
rules.quoted_span: The rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control.
rules.interaction_text: must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control

rules.title: Health and safety violation or removal from rental market
rules.requirement: A tenant may be evicted when the landlord must board up, demolish, or abate health and safety violations, correct an illegal occupancy, or a government agency takes the property off the rental market. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three months before filing and the tenant cannot be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three months before filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants of properties with substantial health and safety violations, illegal occupancies, or property removed from the rental market by a governmental agency.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three months before filing a suit for eviction. The tenant can’t be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for illegal occupancy evictions
rules.requirement: A tenant evicted to correct an illegal occupancy is entitled to relocation assistance equal to six times the monthly rent, paid by the landlord at least five days before removal; otherwise the municipality's revolving fund may pay and the landlord must repay.
rules.key_value: six times the tenant’s monthly rent
rules.coverage_text: Tenants evicted under the illegal occupancy cause.
rules.penalty: If no municipal relocation fund exists and the landlord does not pay on time, interest accrues on the unpaid balance at 18% per year until paid; the amount due is a lien on the property.
rules.quoted_span: Any tenant evicted under G 3) (illegal occupancy) is entitled to relocation assistance in an amount equal to six times the tenant’s monthly rent.

rules.title: Permanent retirement of property from residential use
rules.requirement: A landlord who wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential use may file for eviction after serving a Notice to Quit at least 18 months before filing, and no action may be taken until the lease expires.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least 18 months before filing
rules.coverage_text: Buildings or mobile home parks being permanently retired from residential use.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply where the circumstances in section (G) apply.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months prior to filing the suit for eviction.

rules.title: Refusal to accept reasonable lease changes
rules.requirement: At lease expiration a landlord may propose reasonable but substantial changes; if the tenant refuses after written notice the landlord may file for eviction and the court decides reasonableness. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month before filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants whose lease has expired and who refuse reasonable changes to lease terms.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month before filing suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(i)).

rules.title: Habitual late payment or continuous nonpayment
rules.requirement: If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late after a written Notice to Cease, the landlord may file for eviction after a Notice to Quit served at least one month before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month before filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants who habitually pay late or continuously fail to pay rent.
rules.quoted_span: If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month before filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(j)).

rules.title: Conversion to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership
rules.requirement: A landlord converting a building or mobile home park to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership may file for eviction after serving a Notice to Quit at least three years before filing, and no action may be taken until the lease expires. Courts may grant up to five one-year stays if comparable housing is not offered.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three years before filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants in buildings or mobile home parks being converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership of two or more units or sites.
rules.exemptions: No action for possession against a senior citizen or disabled tenant with protected tenancy status under the Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act of 1992 while that status is in effect.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be ser ved on the tenant at least three years before filing a suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(k)).
rules.interaction_text: The landlord must comply with the regulations governing conversion to condominiums and cooperatives, before a warrant for possession shall be issued.

rules.title: Post-conversion sale to buyer seeking personal occupancy
rules.requirement: An owner of a converted or converting building may evict a tenant whose tenancy began after the master deed was recorded when the unit is sold to a buyer who will personally occupy it, only if the tenant was given a statement of the conversion; a Notice to Quit must be served at least two months before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least two months before filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants whose initial tenancy began after the master deed, cooperative agreement or subdivision plat was recorded in a condominium, cooperative or fee simple building.
rules.quoted_span: However, no action shall be brought against a tenant under paragraph one (1) of this subsection unless the tenant was given a statement, informing the tenant that the property is being converted. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least two months prior to filing suit for eviction.

rules.title: Owner of three or fewer condo/co-op units seeking occupancy
rules.requirement: An owner of three or fewer condominium or cooperative units may evict a tenant whose tenancy began after the master deed was recorded in order to personally occupy the unit or sell it to a buyer who will, after a Notice to Quit served at least two months before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least two months before filing
rules.coverage_text: Owners of three or fewer condominium or cooperative units.
rules.quoted_span: 2) The landlord may file for eviction, if the owner of three or less condominium or cooperative units seeks to evict a tenant whose initial tenancy began, by rental, after the master deed or agreement establishing the cooperative was recorded, because the owner seeks to personally occupy the unit, or has contracted to sell the unit to a buyer who seeks to personally occupy it and the contract for sale calls for the unit to be vacant at the time of closing.

rules.title: Owner of building with three or fewer units seeking occupancy
rules.requirement: An owner of a building with three or fewer residential units may evict to personally occupy a unit or sell it to a buyer who will, after a Notice to Quit served at least two months before filing; no action until the lease expires.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least two months before filing
rules.coverage_text: Buildings with three residential units or less.
rules.quoted_span: 3) The landlord may file for eviction, if the owner of a building with three residential units or less seeks to personally occupy a unit, or has contracted to sell the residential unit to a buyer who wishes to personally occupy it and the contract fo r sale calls for the unit to be vacant at the time of closing. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least two months prior to filing suit for eviction.

rules.title: Tenancy based on employment
rules.requirement: If a tenant's occupancy is conditioned on employment by the landlord (such as superintendent or janitor) and the employment ends, the landlord may file for eviction after a Notice to Quit served three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit three days before filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants whose occupancy is conditioned on employment by the landlord.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(m)).

rules.title: Conviction of a drug offense committed on the property
rules.requirement: A landlord may file for eviction if the tenant was convicted of or pleaded guilty to drug offenses on the property and is not completing a drug rehabilitation program, or lets such a person reside there; suit must be brought within two years and a Notice to Quit served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days before filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants convicted of drug offenses on the property or who let such persons occupy the premises.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to a tenant allowing a juvenile found delinquent due to use or possession of drugs to reside at the property; not applicable if the person completed or is participating in a drug rehabilitation program.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(n)).

rules.title: Conviction of assaulting or threatening the landlord, family, or employees
rules.requirement: A landlord may file for eviction if the tenant was convicted of or pleaded guilty to assault or terrorist threats against the landlord, family or employees, or knowingly lets such a person reside there; suit must be brought within two years and a Notice to Quit served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days before filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants convicted of assault or terrorist threats against the landlord, landlord's family or employees.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three day s prior to filing a suit for (N.J.S.A. 2A-18-61.1(o)).

rules.title: Civil liability for involvement in criminal activities
rules.requirement: A landlord may file for eviction if a civil court finds the tenant liable for theft on the premises, assaults or threats against the landlord, family or employees, or illegal drug activity on the premises; suit must be brought within two years and a Notice to Quit served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days before filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants found liable in civil proceedings for listed criminal activities.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to a tenant allowing a juvenile found delinquent due to the use or possession of drugs to reside at the property.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(p)).

rules.title: Conviction for theft of property
rules.requirement: A landlord may file for eviction if the tenant was convicted of or pleaded guilty to theft of property from the landlord or other tenants in the building, or knowingly lets such a person reside there, after a Notice to Quit served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days before filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants convicted of theft from the landlord or other tenants in the same building or complex.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(q)).

rules.title: Human trafficking eviction ground
rules.requirement: A landlord may file for eviction if the tenant is found in a civil action to have committed human trafficking on the premises or knowingly harbors a person engaged in human trafficking; no action may be brought more than two years after the violation terminated.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants found to have committed or harbored human trafficking on the premises.
rules.quoted_span: No action for removal pursuant to this subsection may be brought mor e than two years after the alleged violation has terminated (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(r)).

rules.title: Evictions for owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings
rules.requirement: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings may be removed only by court order on proof of listed causes (holdover, nonpayment, disorderly conduct, damage, rule violations, or lease violations with right of re-entry). A three month notice to quit is required for at-will or year-to-year tenancies and one month for month-to-month and other tenancies; a three-day notice applies to disorderly, destructive or rule-violation causes.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings.
rules.quoted_span: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when a court issues an order for eviction.

rules.title: Rooming and boarding house evictions
rules.requirement: Owners of rooming and boarding houses must follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, unless otherwise ordered by the Bureau, and must give at least three working days' notice to the County Welfare Board before starting an eviction.
rules.coverage_text: Residents of rooming and boarding houses (buildings with at least two living units occupied by unrelated persons without private kitchens and bathrooms).
rules.exemptions: Except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau.
rules.quoted_span: The Regulations Governing Rooming and Boarding Houses, which are enforced by the Bureau of Rooming and Boarding House Standards of the Department of Community Affairs, require owners of rooming and boarding houses to follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau (N.J.A.C. 5:27-3.3(c)).
